title: Identity write request v1
description: Six writes. `fgos identity machine --alias <name>` replaces <stateRoot>/machine-alias atomically; the alias must follow the Convention machine-handle kind, changes the handle only, never the machine id, and needs a machine id to exist. `fgos identity project --init|--new [--handle <name>]` writes .fgos/project.json of the main checkout: `--init` mints once and refuses when the file exists (project-id-exists), in a linked worktree (linked-worktree) or when the remote default branch, as last fetched, already tracks the file (project-id-on-remote); `--new` replaces the id on purpose (a fork split) and skips the last two checks. The handle follows the Convention project-handle kind and defaults to the slug of the folder name. Nothing else ever writes the file. `fgos identity mint <kind> [--release <number>]` mints an id that travels between machines (docs/platform/identity/spec.md, section 4a): `work` gives `tsk-<10 base32>` and `backlog` gives `p-<10 base32>` from the kernel's random bytes and writes nothing; `d-adr` and `decision-file` claim the next number of the counter ref `refs/fgos/seq/<kind>` on the project's `origin` (the repository's own ref when it has none), one more than the larger of the counter and the highest number the repository's documents carry, retrying a refused compare-and-swap up to 5 times. `--release <number>` gives a sequence number back, only while it is still the counter's tip. Without a network the claim is refused (`sequence-unreachable`); the format is never changed to work around it. `fgos identity session --register [--role lead:<LANE> [--take]]` puts this session in the machine's local directory (<stateRoot>/identity/sessions/<hash of handle>.json, one file per session): the entry carries the process facts of the agent head (the highest ancestor holding a terminal, never the transient fgos child), absent when no ancestor holds one. `--role` implies registering. Registration is only ever explicit: the bare verb, `session` without flags, hooks and workers never write it. Every write first removes the entries whose head is dead; a live session already holding the handle with another id is refused (`handle-in-use`, handles never change); a role held by another live session is refused (`role-held`) unless `--take` moves it; at 512 entries the write is refused (`directory-full`). `fgos identity session --drop-role lead:<LANE>` removes that role from this session's own entry and from no other (`role-not-held` when it does not hold it, `not-registered` when it has no entry), after which the role resolves `not-found` unless another session holds it. `fgos identity list --prune` removes the entries proven dead (as every write does; an entry whose liveness is unknown is kept) and answers the list.

refusal.title: Identity refusal under --json
refusal.description: What stdout carries when the verb is refused and the caller passed --json: one line, exit 65, the same text on stderr as `fgos: error: <error> [<reason>]`. It is not a fgos.v1 envelope (no `contract`): the error path is not wrapped, success and failure differ by exit code. `reason` is one of the outcome's x-refusals.

candidates.description: The sessions the caller may have meant (not-found), the sessions a name matches (ambiguous), the live sessions holding the role (role-not-held); empty otherwise. Consumers ignore unknown fields: a later rung adds machine and fetchedAt, and the liveness value remote.

outcome.title: Identity write outcome v1
outcome.description: The machine as `identity.read` prints it after an alias write, the project minted with where it went and the command that commits it, the id minted, or the answer to a release.

commit.description: The command that commits the new file by pathspec.

oneOf.description: session registered (the entry as `identity resolve` prints it)

clone.description: Working directory the session registered from.

liveness.description: unknown: the session has no terminal ancestor, so nothing can prove it dead. A dead session is never returned.

oneOf.description: directory after a prune (the list as `identity list` prints it)

released.description: false when somebody claimed after, so the counter stays.
